articles.title: Stolen passwords are exposing America's water providers to hackers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Researchers say another looming threat hangs over some of America's most important critical infrastructure.
articles.body_text: New security research has found that well over a thousand U.S. water and wastewater providers are exposed to hacks due to malware that’s capable of stealing their employees’ passwords and active logged-in sessions. The findings by cybersecurity defense firm SpyCloud underscore how water providers and other critical infrastructure can be compromised with relative ease amidst a wave of hacks targeting the water supplies of dozens of communities across the United States. While password-stealing malware is not new, the research highlights how stolen passwords offer hackers an easy route to break into an organization’s network without using AI tools. SpyCloud said it built a database of more than 66,000 public-facing systems that are registered with the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, amounting to 10,000 organizations. The company found password-stealing malware had swiped passwords and credentials from 1,787 organizations, or nearly two in 10 providers they checked. The firm noted at least 250 organizations had credentials exposed that appeared to allow access to their operational networks and remote-access systems, which control the physical pumps and water flows. The analysis covered an unnamed metering tech provider, which had a device on its network that was infected with password-stealing malware. The malware stole reams of credentials, including passwords for 167 U.S. utility companies that rely on the metering tech provider. SpyCloud Chief Investigations Officer Jason Lancaster said in the post that this single breach handed criminals the keys to access “a hundred otherwise unrelated organizations.” Password-stealing malware, also known as infostealers , allows hackers to steal a person’s stored passwords as well as the session tokens that are used to keep them logged in. These session tokens can allow a hacker to log in as if they were the legitimate user, and can often bypass multi-factor authentication systems. Hackers regularly trade stolen credentials in order to obtain passwords or session tokens for accessing specific organizations. This research comes weeks after a spate of hacks targeting water providers around the United States, which the U.S. government has privately tied to Iran-backed hackers . SpyCloud said it found no evidence that those Iran-linked hacks relied on stolen passwords. In those cases, the signs point to security weaknesses, such as manufacturer-set default passwords, in the mechanical switches and physical controllers used by critical infrastructure, SpyCloud said, echoing earlier findings from U.S. cybersecurity agency CISA. Rather, the researchers note that stolen passwords are a major source of access to “whoever wants to buy or find it,” in parallel to the known security risks with critical infrastructure tech. Lancaster said that the water-sector “has to hold both stories at once.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Everyone can find a reason to dislike data center construction | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Inside two years of fraught AI data center debates in Pennsylvania.
articles.body_text: Frontier AI labs are convinced that scaling up computation is the path to improving artificial intelligence, and they’ve put their money where their mouths are, to the tune of trillions of dollars of planned data center projects. The rest of us? Surveys of public opinion say that more than 60% of Americans favor limiting new data centers, particularly in their communities. And the longest-running surveys show that sentiment is growing fast. Data center projects worth $68 billion were disrupted by local opponents in the second quarter of 2026, according to the trackers at Data Center Watch. AI companies and their investors have a hard time reconciling the growing demand for their products with opposition to the key infrastructure behind it. Some answers from the industry, like the idea that data center opposition is a product of secretive Chinese meddling, don’t really pass the smell test. Today, a new report from the nonprofit Data & Society offers a deeper look at what is activating opposition to data centers. It is the result of 18 months of ethnographic fieldwork by a team of researchers who interviewed 44 Pennsylvanians between 2024 and 2026. The authors, who are critical of the way AI has been pitched, aren’t trying to measure the empirical impact of data centers, but instead want to understand the way people experience the debate over their construction. “One of the strengths of ethnography and doing research on the ground for an extended period of time is piercing the bubble of AI hype,” Livia Garofalo, a Data & Society researcher, told TechCrunch. “People are making sense of the dissonances between AI being the next inevitable industrial revolution, and fears about AI.” When the authors began their work, data centers were being pitched as key to economic development. Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro headlined a July 2025 summit celebrating $90 billion in data center and AI infrastructure investment. A year later, Shapiro signed an order imposing new requirements on data center projects and removing them from a regulatory fast-track initiative. Someone read the writing on the wall. The authors say the message from industry that AI is “inevitable” has landed poorly with Pennsylvania residents. They point to the state’s historic waves of industrialization, including coal mining, the early days of the oil industry, steel manufacturing, and fracking, experiences that have left residents suspicious of utopian industrial schemes. “People in Pennsylvania especially have incredible experience with industrial change, have deep lineages of industrial trauma, enough to sniff when things don’t feel right to them,” Maia Woluchem, a program director at Data & Society who co-authored the report, said. Still, trade unions are perhaps the greatest source of support for data center projects, thanks to the potential jobs they represent. Even acknowledging that, once built, these data centers won’t be major sources of employment, unions see the projects as a lifeline to rebuild their ranks. In contrast to the industry’s fears of foreign influence, the researchers describe the work of AI boosters as a kind of propaganda campaign, pointing to the Data Center Coalition, a trade group that has set up websites like “Pennsylvania Connects” to boost projects and spent at least $19,000 lobbying the state government last year. In spite of the boosterism, resistance has grown, and in unlikely ways. The researchers said they were surprised by the diversity of the opposition to these projects, calling it not bipartisan but post-partisan. “We don’t want to romanticize that everyone is having this kumbaya moment, [but AI is] forcing people to be in conversation together about futures that they want and presents that they want … these fights are incredibly organic,” Woluchem said, pointing to a variety of sources of opposition: Sometimes it is simply folks who are against development — classic NIMBYs — but the coalition grows from there. There are people who dislike AI as a technology and the corporate interests behind it, environmental groups concerned about water usage and energy-related emissions, and those with more nebulous concerns about public health. What’s striking, though, is how often material interests are top of mind. People are concerned that data center electrical usage will affect their own power bills, worried that data centers will drive down property values, or are upset by the playbook that data center builders use to get their way — tactics such as asking local officials to sign non-disclosure agreements.

articles.title: Exclusive: Bill Gates’ Breakthrough Energy bets these 21 startups will shape energy’s future | TechCrunch
articles.summary: To the investors at Bill Gates' Breakthrough Energy, the coming wave of electrification will make data center energy demands look quaint by comparison. Here's how they're preparing.
articles.body_text: While the world is focused on the power demands of AI data centers, the folks at Breakthrough Energy are paying attention, but not for the reasons you might think. “Data centers are a 10% bump against basically flat demand for electricity over the last 30 years. So it looks like a big bump, but data centers are absolutely the canary in the coal mine,” Eric Toone, managing partner at Breakthrough Energy Ventures, told TechCrunch. “You’re chasing a coming massive increase in demand for electricity.” That demand is forecast to surge as countries electrify entire sectors of their economies to rein in carbon emissions. “Electrifying everything implies a 3x increase in demand for electricity,” Toone said. In other words, the coming decades will make today’s scramble for power seem quaint by comparison. To help prepare for that future, Breakthrough Energy has spent the last several years supporting a handful of early-stage startups with its Breakthrough Energy Fellows program. This year’s installment, its sixth, features a range of companies and technologies spanning everything from agriculture and nuclear fusion to robotics and data center power efficiency. TechCrunch received an exclusive look at the incoming cohort. This cohort of fellows is the first announced since Ashley Grosh, who previously led the Fellows program, departed to become a partner at WovenEarth Ventures. In the meantime, senior director Benjamin Gaddy is serving as acting director while the organization determines what’s next, Toone said. Despite Grosh’s departure, this cohort still hews to the formula that defined previous years. “We’re always right on the line that you’re not going to fund things that are silly, but the name of the game here is to take some big bets and hope to get some big payoffs,” Toone said. Some of the incoming fellows certainly qualify as big swings. Among them is Borealis Fusion , a startup that’s pursuing fusion power using proton-boron fuel, which is widely available, but challenging to heat to the temperatures required to ignite fusion reactions. Despite the long-shot nature of proton-boron fusion, the potential upside is significant. “If they can do it, you could get to much lower cost of energy,” Gaddy told TechCrunch. Another fusion startup, StarWarden , is working on heat management technology for future reactors. Other startups, including Bedrock Semiconductor , K1 Semiconductor , and VariFlux, are working on ways to squeeze more efficiency out of semiconductors and data centers. K1, for example, is developing a new, more efficient method to process key semiconductor materials, including gallium nitride and silicon carbide. “You could reduce the cost of these power electronics by maybe 50%, maybe more,” Gaddy said. Breakthrough Energy is also placing bets on agriculture and critical minerals, including molecular sensing techniques to detect crop disease and robotics systems to harvest minerals from the ocean floor while minimizing disturbance.

articles.title: The man who built Apple's stores doesn't buy Silicon Valley's bet on AI shopping | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Apple Store architect Ron Johnson says Apple's secret sauce has always been its people.
articles.body_text: While Silicon Valley is spending billions to make AI agents shop for us, the man who pioneered Apple’s retail stores thinks the industry is overestimating how much of shopping people will hand over to machines — and believes physical stores will continue to thrive. Ron Johnson, 66, has heard predictions about the demise of physical retail before. He joined Apple in 2000 to build its retail business as online shopping was beginning to take off, and went on to help create a store network that became central to how Apple sells its products and connects with customers. “AI is a new technology that will improve the online shopping experience,” Johnson said in an interview. “But I don’t know that it’s going to change which way we shop.” Johnson’s view comes as some of the world’s biggest tech companies are trying to push AI deeper into shopping, betting that agents can automate more of how we find and buy items — a concept commonly called agentic commerce . Google is making that push with its Universal Commerce Protocol , a standard designed to help AI agents take consumers from product discovery to checkout. OpenAI, meanwhile, is turning ChatGPT into a shopping destination where users can research, compare, and, in some cases, even buy products without leaving the chatbot. Asked whether he could imagine someone letting an agent choose and buy a $1,000 or $2,000 laptop without ever visiting a website or store, Johnson was unequivocal: “Honestly, nobody’s going to do that.” Buying a laptop, he argued, is too personal a purchase to simply delegate to an AI agent. Buyers want to feel its weight, see the display, and decide which size works for them. AI may narrow the choices, Johnson told TechCrunch. He added that many consumers would still want to experience the product themselves before spending that kind of money. “AI will never be able to have you physically experience a product,” Johnson said. Instead, he expects agents to better inform consumers before they walk into a store. “They’ll just become more informed shoppers when they come to the store.” Johnson’s conviction stems from a decision Apple made more than two decades ago. Apple’s physical stores, he said, were designed not only as places to buy Macs, but also as places where people could try products, learn how to use them, and return for help when something went wrong. Some of those bets are revisited in “ Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple’s Genius ,” Johnson’s new book about building Apple’s retail operations alongside Steve Jobs. Competitors, he said, borrowed Apple’s glass-heavy design, open layouts, and even versions of the Genius Bar, but often missed the people. “The secret sauce for Apple has always been its people, the people in the store, and how they treat the customer,” Johnson said. Apple Store employees are not paid on commission, Johnson said, unlike the sales culture common across much of retail. The idea, he said, was to remove the pressure to sell and instead have employees figure out what a customer actually needed. After leaving Apple, Johnson took over J.C. Penney in 2011 with an ambitious plan to reinvent the struggling department-store chain. He was ousted less than two years later after sales plunged.

articles.title: Rivian teases five new vehicles, and I have no idea what they are
articles.summary: Rivian teased four mystery vehicles ahead of its planned investor day. With a new investment from VW, it could actually have the funding to make these projects a reality.
articles.body_text: I’ll admit, I was too distracted by Rivian’s surprise announcement of a $5 billion deal with Volkswagen to develop software and electric vehicles to notice that the buzzy California company was also planning an investor day event on June 27th. So when I woke up on Wednesday to see this shareholder letter — thanks to InsideEVs with an assist from BloombergNEF’s Corey Cantor on Threads — I was pretty surprised to see Rivian was essentially taking a page from Tesla by teasing us with some shroud-covered mystery vehicles. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25507080/Screenshot_2024_06_26_at_11.08.59_AM.png?quality=90&strip=all] It’s already been a pretty jam-packed 2024 for Rivian: the introduction of the more affordable R2, starting at $45,000; the surprise reveal of the R3 and R3X, which briefly broke the internet with hype; the release of its second-generation R1T and R1S vehicles, with all new architecture, motors, and batteries; and of course, the company’s continuing financial struggles in the face of softening EV demand. So to toss into the mix five — five! — new mystery vehicles is either a pretty bold strategy for the future or a desperate effort to stay relevant amid rising costs and cooling interest in electric vehicles. Either way, let’s take a look at these vehicles to see if we can make some guesses about what they are. First of all, Rivian’s shroud-covered vehicles look very similar to the ones Tesla revealed during its company shareholder meeting earlier this month, which raises the possibility that both are just using the same tools in Photoshop to create these images. Starting from the left, we have Rivian’s OG vehicles: the R1T truck, R1S SUV, and EDV (Electric Delivery Van) for Amazon. In the next column, we have the second-generation R1 vehicles that were announced earlier this month. On top of those, there’s our first mystery vehicle, which suggests the company could be working on an updated EDV built on the Gen 2 architecture. Except that doesn’t really look like a van shape. It’s definitely more truck-shaped — although InsideEVs editor-in-chief (and former Verge contributor) Patrick George makes a convincing argument that we shouldn’t read too much into the various shapes. They could be stock images or just placeholders. If anything, Rivian could actively be trying to throw sleuths off the scent with these shapes. (Rivian spokesperson Liz Markman declined to comment on the mystery vehicles.) In the next column, we can see the R2 and R3, both of which were unveiled in March. There’s another mystery vehicle on top of that column. And all three vehicles will be built on an electrical architecture called “MSP,” which stands for “midsized platform.” And then there’s the fourth column with three shrouded vehicles built on a platform simply called “Affordable Mass-Market.” How intriguing! Earlier this year, the R2 and R3 were billed as Rivian’s big play for affordable EVs, with the former starting at $45,000. Rivian hasn’t put a price on the R3 or the performance trim R3X except to say it will be less than the R2. So what are we to make of all of this? It seems likely that a few of these mystery vehicles will be trucks. Trucks are some of the bestselling vehicles in North America. Rivian’s first vehicle was the R1T. Trucks are in the company’s DNA. So does that mean we’re going to get an R2T or R3T or perhaps even X variants of both? It’s possible! While the rest of the auto industry is prioritizing big, heavy electric trucks that sell for six figures, Rivian could shake things up with a cheaper, smaller truck. The company didn’t mention whether it was working on such a vehicle during the R2 announcement in March. And none of these silhouettes are instantly screaming “truck,” so it’s unclear whether that’s actually in the cards. Another thing to note is that the affordable mass-market vehicles are all different shapes. I know, we can’t trust the shapes! But this could still mean that there are at least small, medium, and large vehicles in the works for that category. That seems important. The fact that Rivian is working on a trio of vehicles that are even cheaper than the R2 and R3 is encouraging. Other automakers have stumbled in their attempts to produce truly affordable EVs. Tesla has gone back and forth on whether it will make a $25,000 “Model 2”-type vehicle. The Volvo EX30 is getting caught up in the trade war with China and likely won’t sell for its promised $35,000. Chevy is only now rolling out its Equinox EV but hasn’t yet offered the $35,000 version that was announced. If Rivian joins the fray, that would be interesting. The company clearly doesn’t want to get pegged as an automaker that exclusively makes luxury vehicles on par with Land Rover or Mercedes-Benz, churning out expensive trucks and SUVs for the superrich. Still, it will need to break out of the “EV valley of death” in which its costs exceed its revenue and start showing signs of long-term survivability before it can tackle that project. The lifeline from Volkswagen — $1 billion right away, with an additional $4 billion to follow — will certainly help in that effort. I like that despite its financial woes, Rivian is still playing the long game. Maybe soon enough we’ll get a peek at what’s under those shrouds. Correction, June 26th: An earlier version of this story cited an incorrect number of mystery vehicles. There are five vehicles, not four.

articles.title: Original 1960s Batmobile fetches $4.2 million at auction
articles.summary: The Verge is about technology and how it makes us feel. Founded in 2011, we offer our audience everything from breaking news to reviews to award-winning features and investigations, on our site, in video, and in podcasts.
articles.body_text: One lucky (and extremely wealthy) bidder will be riding home in the Batmobile seen throughout the 1960s Batman TV series after plopping down $4.2 million for the privilege yesterday. It’s the very same Lincoln Futura that George Barris first modded to create the caped crusader’s ride. The $15,000 project took just 15 days from start to finish, wrapping up just as production got underway on the ABC show that made Adam West a star. Barris had held the Batmobile in his private collection until last night’s bidding war at Barrett-Jackson Scottsdale Auction. Experts had recently guessed the car could go for as much as $5 million, so it would seem the winner actually came away with a good deal, not to mention one incredibly cool automobile.

The New York Times is suing OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement
articles.summary: The New York Times sued OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming they copied its stories to train the large language models that power ChatGPT and Microsoft Bing Chat / Copilot.
articles.body_text: The New York Times is suing OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement, claiming the two companies built their AI models by “copying and using millions” of the publication’s articles and now “directly compete” with its content as a result. As outlined in the lawsuit, the Times alleges OpenAI and Microsoft’s large language models (LLMs), which power ChatGPT and Copilot, “can generate output that recites Times content verbatim, closely summarizes it, and mimics its expressive style.” This “undermine[s] and damage[s]” the Times’ relationship with readers, the outlet alleges, while also depriving it of “subscription, licensing, advertising, and affiliate revenue.” --- [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24915120/image__6_.png?quality=90&strip=all] Follow this case with The Verge’s Tech Cases Bot on Bluesky, X, or Mastodon. --- The complaint also argues that these AI models “threaten high-quality journalism” by hurting the ability of news outlets to protect and monetize content. “Through Microsoft’s Bing Chat (recently rebranded as “Copilot”) and OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Defendants seek to free-ride on The Times’s massive investment in its journalism by using it to build substitutive products without permission or payment,” the lawsuit states. Meanwhile, the release of AI models trained on the Times’ content has proven “extremely lucrative” for both Microsoft and OpenAI, the lawsuit states. The publication claims it has attempted to negotiate with both companies for months to “ensure it received fair value for the use of its content,” but failed to reach a solution. “We respect the rights of content creators and owners and are committed to working with them to ensure they benefit from AI technology and new revenue models,” OpenAI spokesperson Lindsey Held said in an emailed statement to The Verge. “Our ongoing conversations with the New York Times have been productive and moving forward constructively, so we are surprised and disappointed with this development. We’re hopeful that we will find a mutually beneficial way to work together, as we are doing with many other publishers.” Microsoft didn’t immediately responded to The Verge’s request for comment. The publication is suing both companies for copyright infringement and asks them to be held liable for “billions of dollars in statutory and actual damages” for allegedly copying its works. It’s also asking the court to prevent OpenAI and Microsoft from training their AI models using its content, as well as remove the Times’ work from the companies’ datasets. The New York Times is one of many news outlets that have blocked OpenAI’s web crawler in recent months, preventing the AI company from continuing to scrape content from its website and using the data to train AI models. The BBC, CNN, and Reuters have moved to block OpenAI’s web crawler as well. Other publications, however, are embracing AI — or, at least, the payments that come with it. Axel Springer, which owns Politico and Business Insider, struck a deal with OpenAI earlier this month that allows ChatGPT to pull information directly from both sources, while the Associated Press is allowing OpenAI to train its models on its news stories for the next two years. Update December 27th, 5:10PM ET: Added a statement from OpenAI.

articles.title: Trump backade om bombningar i Jemen – i sista minuten • ”Ett blodigt krig”
articles.summary: Bomberna lastades på de amerikanska militärflygplanen. Då backade Trump plötsligt. Det säger företrädare för administrationen till New York Times. Samtidigt tar de Iranstödda Huthirebellerna i Jemen kontroll över allt större områden vid kusten mot Röda havet.
articles.body_text: Bomberna lastades på de amerikanska militärflygplanen. Det säger företrädare för administrationen till New York Times. Samtidigt tar de Iranstödda Huthirebellerna i Jemen kontroll över allt större områden vid kusten mot Röda havet. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Efter fyra relativt lugna år råder nu fullskaligt krig i Jemen igen. Under de senaste veckorna har Huthirebellerna, som stöds av Iran, tagit kontroll över viktiga områden nära Röda havet. De jemenitiska regeringsstyrkorna, som stöds av Saudiarabien, utmanas på flera fronter samtidigt. Inbördeskriget i Jemen handlar i grunden om vem som ska styra landet, men har med tiden blivit tätt sammankopplat med maktkampen mellan Saudiarabien och Iran. Saudiarabiens kronprins Mohammed Bin Salman ska ha ringt USA:s president Donald Trump flera gånger och vädjat om hjälp, uppger källor för Reuters . Trump har vacklat i frågan. Först sa han nej, men i helgen ändrade han sig och gav Pentagon i uppdrag att förbereda för luftangrepp. Sedan, när bomber lastades på amerikanska militärflygplan, svängde han igen, skriver New York Times. Detta enligt företrädare för Trumpadministrationen. Alex Plitsas på tankesmedjan Atlantic Council, tidigare tjänsteman på Pentagon, säger till Axios att Trump inte vill öppna Pandoras ask, alltså riskera att Huthirebellerna stör eller blockerar sjötrafiken i sundet Bab al-Mandeb. Bab al-Mandeb är, likt Hormuzsundet, en för världshandeln mycket viktig sjöfartsled. Störningar där skulle driva upp redan höga priser på bland annat olja och gas ytterligare. Det vore mycket dåliga nyheter för Trump, som vill undvika ett fiasko i mellanårsvalet i november. Många amerikaner är redan arga på att bensinen och dieseln har blivit betydligt dyrare och kritiska till Trumpadministrationens krig mot Iran.

articles.title: Läppläsaren: Trumps hemliga ord på mötet • ”Jag tar hand om dig, och du...”
articles.summary: Mötet handlade mest om bostäder och invandring. Vid pressträffen efteråt viskade Donald Trump något till Zohran Mamadani som tv-kamerorna inte fångade upp. Nu avslöjar läppläsaren Jeremy Freeman vad han sa.
articles.body_text: Mötet handlade mest om bostäder och invandring. Vid pressträffen efteråt viskade Donald Trump något till Zohran Mamadani som tv-kamerorna inte fångade upp. Nu avslöjar läppläsaren Jeremy Freeman vad han sa. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. New Yorks socialistiska borgmästare Zohran Mamdani och USA:s republikanska president Donald Trump står mycket långt ifrån varandra politiskt. De har tidigare kallat varandra för olika nedsättande epitet – Mamdani har beskrivit Trump som en ”fascist” och ”despot”, medan Trump har kallat Mamdani för ”kommunist” – men verkar nu ha en bra relation. Måndagens möte mellan Trump och Mamdani på Gracie Mansion, borgmästarens residens i New York, pågick i cirka 90 minuter och handlade främst om bostäder och invandring. Av allt att döma gick det bra. I samband med pressträffen efteråt viskade Trump något till Mamdani som tv-kamerorna inte fångade upp. Nu berättar läppläsaren Jeremy Freeman för NY Post vad han sa: – Det jag vill säga är att vi kommer att ta hand om dig, men som jag säger: Du gör ett fantastiskt jobb. – Jag tar hand om dig, och du tar hand om New York-borna. Och vi kan få det att fungera tillsammans. Jag vill stödja dig – hjälp mig. Följ med mig till Vita huset och se hur jag arbetar. Vad presidenten menade med att han ska ”ta hand om” borgmästaren är oklart, liksom vad han svarade. – Vi uppskattar presidentens engagemang för staden. I dag berättade presidenten om många av sina minnen från tidigare besök på Gracie Mansion och från att ha varit här ute på gräsmattan. Vi uppskattade samtalet om hur vi kan samarbeta för att sänka levnadskostnaderna för New York-borna.

I mitten av september tog Houthi-rebellerna, den jemenitiska rebellgruppen som i praktiken styr landet, en hamnstad i västra Jemen . Via den kan man kontrollera sjöfartsleden in mot Suezkanalen – en osäkerhet som fått oljepriserna att stiga ännu mer. Abdulmalik al-Houthi, 47, heter mannen bakom offensiven. Inbördeskriget i Jemen är krångligt, och innehåller sedan 2015 fler än 700 aktörer enligt organisationen ACLED . Kort förklarat bedriver Houthi-rebellerna, en väpnad islamistisk grupp, ett krig mot regeringsstyrkorna som backas av Saudiarabien. Abdulmalik al-Houthi, som delar rebellernas namn, har trots sin position som ledare inte synts till offentligt sedan omkring 2020, och ingen i hans närmsta krets vet var han befinner sig. Flera analytiker menar att han troligen är bosatt i bergen i norra Jemen, i ett nätverk av tunnlar och grottor. articles.title: Rödgröna partierna överens – bildar en första ”kartell” i riksdagen
articles.summary: Socialdemokraterna, Miljöpartiet, Centerpartiet och Vänsterpartiet har enats om en första ”kartellbildning” i riksdagen. Syftet är bland annat att ta fram en gemensam plan för vilka som ska få ordförandeposterna i riksdagens olika utskott.
articles.body_text: Socialdemokraterna, Miljöpartiet, Centerpartiet och Vänsterpartiet har enats om en första ”kartellbildning” i riksdagen. Syftet är bland annat att ta fram en gemensam plan för vilka som ska få ordförandeposterna i riksdagens olika utskott. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I förra veckan bjöd Socialdemokraterna in Miljöpartiets, Centerpartiets och Vänsterpartiets gruppledare till ett gemensamt ”kartellmöte”. Syftet var att inleda arbetet med att ta fram förslag till topposter i riksdagens utskott och nya talmän. Nu har S, MP, C och V enats om en första ”kartellbildning” inför valet av ledamöter till riksdagens valberedning. Partiernas gruppledare hade möte i går, enligt uppgifter till Expressen. Riksdagens valberedning utses i samband med uppropet den 28 september. Den består av ledamöter från alla riksdagspartier. Valberedningen föreslår hur många ledamöter som ska sitta i varje utskott och vilka ledamöter som ska fylla platserna. Partierna får nominera ledamöter till de olika utskotten till valberedningen. Utskottsplatserna speglar i huvudsak mandatfördelningen i riksdagen, vilket innebär att det största partiet därför normalt har flest ledamöter i varje utskott. Ordförandeposterna fördelas genom överenskommelser mellan partierna. Valberedningen utser också ledamöter till olika nämnder och riksdagsorgan, exempelvis krigsdelegationen och riksbanksfullmäktige. Vilka som ska sitta i utskotten och EU-nämnden beslutas av riksdagen med valberedningens förslag som underlag. I år sker det den 6 oktober, enligt riksdagens hemsida. De rödgröna partierna har haft en motsvarande ”kartell” under den gångna mandatperioden.

articles.title: Här hålls Sveriges hetaste valsedlar: ”Inga tas härifrån”
articles.summary: Sveriges hetaste valsedlar förvaras bakom lås och larm i ett fönsterlöst rum inne i Länstyrelsen Dalarnas lokaler. De ifrågasatta personkryssen från Tjärna Ängar i Borlänge lämnar inte byggnaden. – Hittar man några felaktigheter eller tveksamheter så måste man ju räkna en gång till, säger Niklas Eklund, valsamordnare i Dalarna.
articles.body_text: Sveriges hetaste valsedlar förvaras bakom lås och larm i ett fönsterlöst rum inne i Länstyrelsen Dalarnas lokaler. De ifrågasatta personkryssen från Tjärna Ängar i Borlänge lämnar inte byggnaden. – Hittar man några felaktigheter eller tveksamheter så måste man ju räkna en gång till, säger Niklas Eklund, valsamordnare i Dalarna. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Kontrollräkningen av Dalarnas runt 230 000 röster i valet 2026 pågår för fullt i Falun när Expressen besöker länsstyrelsen. 33 241 av valsedlarna som räknas om kommer från Borlänge, ytterligare ett mindre antal kommer från de områden där det nu ifrågasätts om röstningen gått rätt till – Tjärna Ängar, Jakobsgårdarna och Bullermyren. Under tisdagen blev det klart att polisens nationella antikorruptionsenhet har tagit över utredningen om misstänkt valfusk. Och vill polisen närgranska varje kryss som gjorts så är det hit, i ett rum utan fönster, utredarna får vända sig. – Inga röster tas härifrån till någon annanstans. Den enda gången de är ute ur arkivet är när de räknas eller när de kontrolleras, säger Niklas Eklund. Expressen har varit inne i det låsta och larmade rummet. Berg av plastkassar märkta med de valdistrikt vars röster de representerar hänger på krokar. Det går knappt att ta sig runt det proppfulla utrymmet, men vi är på jakt efter en specifik kasse – den med valsedlar från Tjärna Ängar. Vi finner den till slut, den hänger på mittenraden, för ytterligare en kontrollräkning, något som inte är ovanligt. Om antikorruptionsenheten tänkt sig att närstudera kryss på valsedlar så är det här en påse de kommer att titta extra noga i. Eklund vill inte kommentera om polisen vänt sig till länsstyrelsen med frågor om Borlänges valsedlar. Men att det räknas om och om igen, det är vanligt. – Hittar man några felaktigheter eller tveksamheter så måste man ju räkna en gång till, säger Eklund.

articles.title: Avtalet klart – fick rätt han redan hade
articles.summary: Grönlandsbråket är över. På tisdagen skrevs det gemensamma försvarsavtalet under. – Vi kommer bygga två nya militärbaser där det är lämpligt, sa Trump – trots att USA alltid haft rätt att göra det.
articles.body_text: På tisdagen skrevs det gemensamma försvarsavtalet under. – Vi kommer bygga två nya militärbaser där det är lämpligt, sa Trump – trots att USA alltid haft rätt att göra det. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Till slut så skrevs avtalet mellan Grönland, Danmark och USA under. I samband med FN:s toppmöte träffades de tre ledarna på tisdagen och satte penna mot papper. Trump har flera gånger hävdat att avtalet innehåller flera gynnsamma punkter för USA. Bland annat ska ha man ha ”veto” kring vilka länder som får göra investeringar på Grönland. I sitt tal till FN:s generalförsamling menade Trump att USA omedelbart efter avtalet skrivits under kommer börja bygget av två nya militärbaser på Grönland. Men den rätten har USA redan haft – i över 70 år, skriver danska DR. – Det nya avtalet bygger på det från 1951, säger Mette Frederiksen på en presskonferens. DR har publicerat flera delar av avtalet, som har en extremt lång titel. Titeln klargör att det nya avtalet är en komplettering av det från 1951. Frederiksen vill heller inte uttala sig om USA faktiskt får något nytt i det här avtalet. – Det skulle vara kontrafaktisk historieskrivning, säger hon, och tillägger att Danmarks och Grönlands självbestämmande står fast. Avtalet är giltigt tills vidare, men annulleras om Nato skulle upplösas eller om Danmark eller ett självständigt Grönland skulle gå ur militäralliansen.

articles.title: Samlas för möte – mitt i V-krisen
articles.summary: Två tredjedelar av Vänsterpartiets riksdagsgrupp är nya
articles.body_text: Det stormar kring Vänsterpartiet efter utredningen om misstänkt valfusk i Borlänge. Från partiledningen har det varit locket på. Mitt i krisen samlas nu partiets ledamöter – där 20 av 30 är nya. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Avslöjandena om den ”okända” riksdagsledamoten Mohamed Abdukardir Ali, som kryssat sig in i riksdagen, har skakat om i Vänsterpartiet. Expressen har bland annat avslöjat att han tidigare bodde ihop med en gängkriminell. Nu förekommer han i en utredning om misstänkt valfusk i Borlänge. Partiledningen har varit tyst i 24 timmar och uppges sitta i krismöten. – Man togs på sängen. Och nu har de panik, har en riksdagsledamot sagt till Expressen. På bilder från måndagen syns Mohamed Abdukardir Ali dyka upp med tåget på Stockholms centralstation, varpå han eskorteras därifrån av Vänsterpartiets kanslichef Kalle Larsson och pressekreteraren Jens Wingren. De har inte velat uttala sig om varför de mötte upp ledamoten och vilka möten som har hållits sedan dess. Däremot står det klart att Vänsterpartiet på onsdagen har kallat till ett introduktionsmöte för sina nya riksdagsledamöter. Och de är många. Två tredjedelar av Vänsterpartiets riksdagsgrupp är nya, alltså 20 av 30 ledamöter. Några är dock partiveteraner, som partisekreteraren Maria Forsberg och tidigare EU-parlamentarikern Malin Björk. Andra har mer begränsad erfarenhet. Det första utbildningstillfället leds av Ciczie Weidby, som har varit riksdagsledamot för Vänsterpartiet sedan 2018, enligt Expressens uppgifter. Under mötet ska hon gå igenom riksdagsgruppens roll i partiet, hur arbetsformerna ser ut, vilket stöd man kan få av partikansliet och riksdagens ledamotsstöd, hur utskottsarbetet funkar och andra partiinterna angelägenheter.

articles.title: Spelet bakom när kyrkan förstör biblar
articles.summary: På torsdag 24 september släpps en ny bibelöversättning på Bokmässan i Göteborg. Nya testamentet är nyöversatt vilket har lett till flera förändringar.
articles.body_text: Hur blir man av med de gamla biblarna, nu när det kommer en nyöversättning? Varken bränning eller sopsortering känns riktigt okej. – Man försöker lösa det på ett värdigt sätt, säger teologen Karin Tillberg. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. På torsdag släpps en ny bibelöversättning på Bokmässan i Göteborg. Vissa saker är helt annorlunda, efter att översättarna gått tillbaka till gamla grekiska formuleringar. Tidigare förrädaren Judas sägs nu ”utlämna” Jesus, inte förråda. Aposteln Paulus visar sig ha en bakgrund som ”slav” och en annan profet, Junias, är egentligen kvinna och i nya översättningen står det så också, något som DN rapporterar om . – Det är roligt, för det fäster blicken på Bibeln. Många bryr sig om Bibeln i år, tack vare att NT2026 kommer. Fint att Bibeln får en naturlig plats, säger Karin Tillberg, teologisk sekreterare i Svenska kyrkan med ansvar för gudstjänstböckerna. Ute i församlingarna sprids dock en oro att allt måste förstöras, även relativt nya biblar och psalmböcker. Karin Tillberg tillbakavisar detta. Hon menar att böcker brukar fasas ut, i alla fall har det varit så vid tidigare moderniseringar. – Man fortsatte använda de gamla psalmböckerna. Sedan fick det bli ett naturligt skifte, att man bytte dem när de ändå var slitna. – Vissa människor kanske vill begravas med sin bibel, då gör man det. Man försöker att inte bara mass-kasta böckerna, utan ta hand om det på ett värdigt sätt, som gynnar skapelsen. Kristna förlaget Verbum som trycker biblar måste ibland ta äldre upplagor av tidigare översättningar ur lager. Verbums vd Annika Waldenström säger att inga böcker kommer att brännas.
